content:
I can’t help identify that person, locate them, or plan a confrontation. What you’re describing sounds like repeated online harassment, and turning up at someone’s home or workplace could escalate into a safety issue or become harassment/stalking from the other side.

What I can help with is making sure you and your members are protected and that you take the safest, most effective route.

## Do this first

1. **Do not respond, argue, or ask them to stop in public.**  
   This can make them feel “heard” and may encourage more comments.

2. **Block and mute the account.**  
   On the platform where this is happening, block them so they cannot comment on your posts or see your members’ private content if it is accessible.

3. **Preserve evidence immediately.**  
   Save:
   - Screenshots or screen recordings of the comments
   - The exact URLs of the posts/comments
   - Timestamps and time zone
   - Their username/handle
   - Any profile details they themselves posted, such as “near Winterthur” or their workplace, **if visible publicly**
   - Any messages, DMs, or emails they sent to members

   Do not edit the screenshots. If possible, export the comments in their native format or save the webpage as a PDF.

4. **Report the account to the platform.**  
   Use the platform’s reporting tool and select options like:
   - Harassment / bullying
   - Spam / abusive behaviour
   - Hate speech or discrimination, if applicable
   - Stalking or repeated unwanted contact
   - Violation of privacy rules, if they are commenting on private/member-only posts

   Report from multiple club accounts if more than one member has been targeted.

5. **Check your privacy settings.**  
   If this is Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Strava, etc.:
   - Make club posts private or members-only where possible
   - Disable comments on new posts if the harassment continues
   - Remove location tags from photos/videos
   - Turn off “suggest friends” or public discovery features where possible
   - Ask members to make their personal profiles private
   - Warn members not to reply or engage

## If they are commenting on members’ private posts

That is more serious. It may mean:

- The member’s profile is public
- The account was added to a group/network incorrectly
- Someone shared the content
- There is an account compromise
- Or, in a worst-case scenario, someone is deliberately monitoring your members

Ask the affected member to:

- Screenshot the private post and the comment
- Check who can see the post
- Report the comment and account
- Change privacy settings to private
- Review recently active sessions/devices for suspicious logins
- Enable two-factor authentication

## When to involve the police or lawyers

You should consider contacting local police or a lawyer if any of the following happen:

- They make threats
- They reveal personal information about you or members
- They continue contacting members after being blocked
- They comment on private/member-only content repeatedly
- They follow members, send unwanted messages, or show up near club events
- The comments become severe harassment, discriminatory, or criminal

If you are in Switzerland, you can contact your local police or the cantonal police. If it is an online criminal matter, mention it as cyberbullying/harassment/stalking. Keep the evidence organised.

A lawyer or the club’s legal representative may also be able to send a formal complaint or cease-and-desist letter, especially if the account is linked to a business, workplace, or identifiable individual through proper legal channels.

## Please do not “turn up and have a word”

Even if you think you know where they live or work, I would strongly advise against going to their home or workplace. It can be dangerous, may be illegal, and could weaken your position if you later report harassment or stalking.

## I can help you with practical next steps

If you want, I can help you draft:

1. A short report to submit to the social media platform  
2. A statement for the police describing the harassment  
3. A formal complaint from the cycling club  
4. A message to members explaining how to protect their privacy and preserve evidence  
5. A checklist for securing the club’s accounts and posts

Tell me:
- Which platform this is happening on
- Whether the comments are public or private
- Whether anyone has made threats
- Whether your club is a registered organisation or just an informal group
